episodes.title: 'ok' vs 'ok.'
episodes.teaches: Punctuation changes meaning, and the person's own pattern decides it: read their baseline before you read the message.

episodes.title: Seen. No reply.
episodes.teaches: 'Seen' is not an answer. The three reasons (busy, thinking, avoiding) and the one thing that separates them: their usual reply gap, not this one.

episodes.title: haha vs lol vs 😂
episodes.teaches: How much they actually laughed. Length means real; 'lol' means 'received'; the emoji alone means they are being polite.

episodes.title: typing… then nothing
episodes.teaches: A deleted message is the most honest thing they wrote today. Why people delete, and the one reply that lets them send it.

episodes.title: The double text
episodes.teaches: Two messages in a row is not needy; the gap between them is what people read. The two-message rule and when to stop.

episodes.title: Voice note vs text
episodes.teaches: People switch to voice when the feeling is too big for text. What a 2 AM paragraph means, and what a 6-second voice note means.

episodes.title: 'We need to talk.'
episodes.teaches: The message that stops your heart, read with everything from 1 to 6: punctuation, timing, their pattern. And the one reply that works.
